name: Pyramid Texts
material: Carved on walls of pyramid burial chambers at Saqqara
contents: Spells to help the king's soul rise to join the gods and the stars.
summary: The oldest known religious texts in the world; ancestors of the Coffin Texts and the Book of the Dead.

name: Epic of Gilgamesh
when: c. 2100 BCE (Sumerian poems); standard version c. 1200 BCE
where_now: British Museum (Nineveh tablets from Ashurbanipal's library); others in Iraq and elsewhere
contents: King Gilgamesh of Uruk and his friend Enkidu fight monsters; after Enkidu's death Gilgamesh seeks immortality and hears the story of a great flood from Utnapishtim.
summary: Among the oldest surviving great works of literature. The flood tablet, read by George Smith in 1872, caused a sensation for its parallels with Noah.

name: Code of Hammurabi
contents: 282 laws on trade, family, property, wages and crime, with punishments graded by social class ('an eye for an eye' among equals).
summary: One of the most complete early law codes; shows the idea that a king must publish laws so the weak are protected from the strong.

name: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
when: c. 1550 BCE (copy of an older text)
contents: 84 problems on fractions, areas, volumes of granaries and pyramids, and an approximation of π.
summary: The best source on Egyptian mathematics, copied by the scribe Ahmes.

name: Book of the Dead (Papyrus of Ani)
contents: Spells guiding the dead through the underworld, including the weighing of the heart against the feather of Ma'at.
summary: The finest illustrated copy of Egypt's funerary texts.

name: Amarna letters
where_now: British Museum, Berlin, Cairo and others
contents: Letters between pharaohs and kings of Babylon, Mitanni, the Hittites and Canaanite city rulers.
summary: The first archive of international diplomacy.

name: Dead Sea Scrolls
where_now: Israel Museum (Shrine of the Book), Jerusalem
contents: The oldest copies of nearly every book of the Hebrew Bible, plus sectarian rules of a Jewish community at Qumran.
summary: Found by a Bedouin shepherd in 1947, they are about 1,000 years older than previously known Hebrew Bible manuscripts.

name: Rigveda
when: Composed c. 1500–1200 BCE; oral, written manuscripts from c. 1040 CE
material: Oral tradition; birch bark and paper manuscripts
where_now: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune (30 manuscripts on UNESCO Memory of the World)
contents: 1,028 hymns to Agni, Indra, Soma and other deities in ten books (mandalas).
summary: The oldest text in any Indo-European language still used in worship, preserved word-perfectly by oral recitation for over 3,000 years.

name: Upanishads
contents: Philosophical dialogues on Brahman, Atman, karma and liberation.
summary: Foundation of Vedanta philosophy; translated into Persian by Dara Shikoh (1657) and later admired by Schopenhauer.

name: Edicts of Ashoka
material: Inscribed on rocks and polished pillars
where_now: In situ across India, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan
contents: Ashoka describes remorse after Kalinga and urges dhamma: non-violence, respect for all sects, care for animals.
summary: The oldest deciphered Indian writing (deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837).

name: Arthashastra
contents: A manual on statecraft: taxes, espionage, law, war, diplomacy and economy, attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya).
summary: Rediscovered in 1905 by R. Shamasastry from a palm-leaf manuscript.

name: Tolkappiyam and Sangam anthologies
where_now: Rediscovered by U. V. Swaminatha Iyer in the 19th century
contents: Grammar and 2,381 poems of love (akam) and war (puram).
summary: The foundation of Tamil literature.

name: Bakhshali manuscript
contents: Arithmetic and algebra problems with a dot used as a placeholder zero.
summary: Contains among the oldest written uses of a zero symbol.

name: Gilgit manuscripts
contents: Buddhist texts including the Lotus Sutra.
summary: Among the oldest surviving manuscripts in India.

name: Baburnama
where_now: National Museum, New Delhi; British Library
contents: Babur's frank memoir of his life, battles, gardens and flora of India.
summary: The first true autobiography in Islamic literature.

name: Akbarnama
contents: Abul Fazl's official history of Akbar, including the Ain-i-Akbari.
summary: Masterpiece of Mughal painting.

name: Guru Granth Sahib (Kartarpur Bir)
contents: Hymns of the Sikh Gurus and Hindu and Muslim saints.
summary: The living Guru of Sikhism.

name: Oracle bones of the Shang
where_now: Institute of History and Philology, Taipei; Chinese museums
contents: Questions to ancestors about harvests, war and childbirth.
summary: The earliest Chinese writing.

name: Guodian bamboo slips
contents: The oldest versions of the Daodejing and Confucian texts.
summary: Rewrote understanding of early Daoism.

name: Diamond Sutra (Dunhuang)
contents: A Buddhist sutra on emptiness and wisdom.
summary: The oldest dated printed book in the world.

name: Tale of Genji
contents: Prince Genji's loves and the court life of Heian Japan.
summary: Often called the world's first novel.

name: Tripitaka Koreana
contents: The complete Buddhist canon.
summary: The world's most complete and accurate Buddhist canon in Chinese.

name: Jikji
contents: Selected teachings of Buddhist monks.
summary: The oldest surviving book printed with metal movable type.

name: Hunminjeongeum
contents: King Sejong's proclamation and explanation of Hangul.
summary: Introduced the Korean alphabet.

name: Homer's Iliad (Venetus A)
when: Composed c. 750 BCE; Venetus A copied 10th century
contents: The wrath of Achilles in the Trojan War.
summary: The foundation of Western literature.

name: Codex Sinaiticus
where_now: British Library, Leipzig, St Catherine's, St Petersburg
contents: The oldest complete New Testament.
summary: A key witness to the Christian Bible.

name: Archimedes Palimpsest
contents: Lost works of Archimedes, including The Method.
summary: Imaging revealed Archimedes' early ideas of calculus.

name: Book of Kells
contents: The four Gospels illuminated with Celtic designs.
summary: A masterpiece of Insular art.

name: Beowulf manuscript
contents: The hero Beowulf fights Grendel, his mother and a dragon.
summary: The longest Old English epic.

name: Domesday Book
contents: A survey of land and property in England.
summary: An unmatched record of medieval society.

name: Magna Carta
contents: Limits on royal power and the right to due process.
summary: A symbol of the rule of law.

name: Gutenberg Bible
contents: The Latin Vulgate Bible.
summary: The first major book printed with movable metal type in Europe.

name: Leonardo's Codex Leicester
contents: Notes on water, fossils and astronomy.
summary: Shows Renaissance science.

name: Voynich manuscript
contents: Illustrations of plants, stars and bathers in an unknown script.
summary: Still undeciphered.

name: Birmingham Quran manuscript
contents: Parts of surahs 18–20.
summary: Among the oldest Quran fragments.

name: House of Wisdom translations
contents: Arabic translations of Greek, Persian and Indian science.
summary: Preserved Aristotle, Galen and Indian mathematics.

name: Al-Khwarizmi's Algebra
contents: Solving equations by completion and balancing.
summary: Gave us 'algebra' and 'algorithm'.

name: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine
contents: Medical encyclopaedia.
summary: Used in Europe until the 17th century.

name: Timbuktu manuscripts
where_now: Ahmed Baba Institute and family libraries
contents: Astronomy, medicine, law and history.
summary: Hundreds of thousands were saved from militants in 2012–13.

name: Kebra Nagast
contents: Solomon, the Queen of Sheba and their son Menelik.
summary: Ethiopia's national epic.

name: Dresden Codex
contents: Venus tables and almanacs.
summary: The best-preserved Maya book.

name: Codex Mendoza
contents: Aztec history, tribute and daily life.
summary: Main source on Aztec society.

name: Popol Vuh
contents: Creation, the Hero Twins and K'iche' kings.
summary: The sacred book of the K'iche' Maya.

name: Florentine Codex
contents: Sahagún's encyclopaedia of Aztec life.
summary: Major ethnographic source.

name: Mahabharata (critical edition manuscripts)
when: Composed c. 400 BCE–400 CE; oldest manuscripts much later
where_now: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune (critical edition from about 1,200 manuscripts)
contents: The epic war between the Pandavas and Kauravas, including the Bhagavad Gita.
summary: At about 100,000 verses, the longest epic poem; the Pune critical edition took 1919–1966.

name: Valmiki Ramayana manuscripts
where_now: Many libraries; oldest dated manuscript from Nepal (1020 CE)
contents: Rama's exile, the abduction of Sita by Ravana and her rescue.
summary: Retold across Asia in hundreds of versions.

name: Kathasaritsagara
contents: An 'ocean of story streams' by Somadeva, including the Vetala tales.
summary: One of the largest story collections in the world.

name: The Art of War (Bamboo slips of Yinqueshan)
contents: Sun Tzu's 13 chapters on strategy; also found with the lost text of Sun Bin.
summary: The oldest copies of the most influential military treatise.

name: Bayeux Tapestry
contents: The Norman Conquest of England, from Harold's oath to the Battle of Hastings.
summary: An embroidered 'comic strip' of a war, with soldiers, horses and Halley's Comet.

name: Iliad and Odyssey papyri
contents: Fragments of Homer's epics from Egyptian rubbish dumps.
summary: Homer was the most copied text in Greek Egypt.

name: Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp
where_now: Dispersed; many in the Met and Tehran
contents: Ferdowsi's epic with 258 paintings.
summary: One of the most lavish illustrated manuscripts ever made.

name: Rajatarangini
contents: Kalhana's chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.
summary: One of the first critical histories in India.

name: Prithviraj Raso
when: Attributed to Chand Bardai; texts from the 16th century
contents: The legendary life of Prithviraj Chauhan.
summary: Mixes history and legend.

name: Padmavat
contents: Malik Muhammad Jayasi's allegorical poem about Queen Padmini and Alauddin Khalji's siege of Chittor.
summary: The source of the Padmini legend.
